note: A widely cited overview for clinical staff, useful as background reading to issue before an audit interview round.
title: Revolutionizing healthcare: the role of artificial intelligence in clinical practice
explain_beginner: This review examines how artificial intelligence is used in clinical care. It says AI can help doctors identify illnesses, choose treatments, and support patients. By studying large amounts of health data, AI can spot patterns and sometimes do better than people on certain tasks. The paper reports possible gains such as greater accuracy, lower costs, saved time, and fewer mistakes. It also mentions care tailored to individuals, better medicine amounts, health planning for groups, online helpers, emotional and mental care, and teaching patients. However, data privacy, unfair bias, and the need for skilled people must be handled. This matters because hospitals need to adopt AI carefully and responsibly.
explain_business: For executives, this review suggests AI can support clinical operations by improving identifying illnesses, choosing treatments, and lab tests. It may raise accuracy, cut costs, save time, and reduce human errors. Practical uses include care tailored to individuals, setting medicine amounts, managing health across groups, guidelines, online helpers, emotional and mental care, and teaching patients. The paper notes effects on trust between patients and doctors. Adoption is not just automation, it should enhance care. The decision it informs is whether and how to introduce AI responsibly. Leaders should plan for data privacy and unfair bias controls, retain skilled people, and equip staff with the knowledge and tools needed for implementation.
explain_practitioner: The authors reviewed indexed literature from PubMed/Medline, Scopus, and EMBASE. They included English articles. Their question was how AI affects healthcare settings and what outcomes follow. The review reports that AI can improve identifying illnesses, choosing treatments, and lab tests. Using large datasets to find patterns, AI may exceed human performance. Reported benefits include higher accuracy, lower costs, time savings, and fewer human errors. Uses include care tailored to individuals, setting medicine amounts, managing health across groups, guidelines, online helpers, emotional and mental care, and teaching patients. The authors conclude AI can assist diagnosis and clinician decisions, but data privacy, unfair bias, and the need for skilled people remain challenges.
